robot.name: Unitree G1
robot.status_notes: Unitree's official shop lists the base G1 with a public price and backorder status; EDU variants require contact or separate configuration.

battery.notes: Official product page describes a quick-release battery.

degrees_of_freedom.notes: Official page lists 23 DoF for base G1 and 23-43 DoF for EDU configurations depending on options.

walking_speed.notes: Official figure, added 2026-10-29 by automated spec fill; walking speed.

hands.description: Base G1 listing has no dexterous hand; EDU options include Dex3-1, a 7-DoF three-finger hand, with optional tactile arrays.
hands.force_feedback: optional tactile arrays listed for EDU hand options; force feedback not independently verified

compute.description: Official page lists secondary development and NVIDIA Jetson Orin for EDU configurations; base model does not include secondary development according to the product table.

actuators.description: Official page lists 6 DoF per leg, 5 DoF per arm, 90 Nm knee torque on base G1, and 120 Nm knee torque on EDU configurations.

manipulation_dexterity.summary: Base G1 has arms but no dexterous hands in the shop configuration; EDU options and academic work show G1-based grasping, tray transport, and manipulation experiments.
caveats: Do not assume the base model includes EDU hands.
Academic task results are not shipped-product autonomy.

autonomy_task_execution.summary: Academic papers report real-G1 behaviors including self-recovery, RGB-based loco-manipulation, tray transport, and structured grasping tasks.
caveats: Research results depend on external algorithms and experimental setups.
No named commercial customer deployment with hours or output was found.

mobility_whole_body_control.summary: Official specs establish a compact biped platform, and research reports real-G1 self-recovery from face-up and face-down falls across varied surfaces.
caveats: No public official walking-speed value found.
Research policies may not ship with the base robot.

perception_scene_understanding.summary: Official specs list depth camera and 3D LiDAR; academic work reports RGB-based loco-manipulation and visual grasping experiments on G1.
caveats: Scene-understanding results come from research systems.

human_interaction.summary: Official specs list a microphone array and speaker, but no strong public evidence of robust conversational interaction was found.
caveats: Audio hardware is not proof of conversational autonomy.

endurance_reliability.summary: Official page lists about 2 hours of runtime and an 8-month base warranty, but no fleet reliability or commercial operating-hour data was found.
caveats: Security research raises separate operational-risk questions.

human_environment_fit.summary: G1 is a compact biped humanoid sized for indoor research and human-designed lab environments, with public research demonstrations on real hardware.
caveats: Industrial or home deployment proof was not found.

deployment_commercial_proof.summary: The robot is publicly sold and appears in academic lab inventories, but no commercial customer deployment with task, hours, or output was found.

accessibility_value.summary: Unitree's official shop lists a 13500 USD base price, making G1 unusually accessible relative to many humanoids; EDU and option pricing is separate or contact-based.
caveats: Price and shop status are time-sensitive.
Shipping, taxes, backorder timing, and EDU options change total cost.

evidence_items.title: Official G1 product specifications
evidence_items.claim: Unitree's official G1 page lists a 1320 mm standing height, about 35 kg weight, about 2 hours runtime, 23 base DoF, depth camera, 3D LiDAR, and base arm payload around 2 kg.
evidence_items.notes: Official product specs; base and EDU variants differ.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Establishes morphology, sensors, and base capabilities.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Official G1 product page lists size, weight, runtime, DoF, sensors, and payload.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Official company specs; base and EDU variants differ.

evidence_items.title: Official shop price and availability
evidence_items.claim: Unitree's official shop lists the G1 base model at 13500 USD with backorder status and separate sales handling for EDU variants.
evidence_items.notes: Price and stock status are time-sensitive.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Strong accessibility evidence, not deployment evidence.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Official shop lists base G1 price and order/backorder status.

evidence_items.title: Launch release and initial price/spec claims
evidence_items.claim: Unitree's launch release introduced G1 and gave an initial price claim of about 16000 USD excluding tax and shipping, plus sensor and battery details.
evidence_items.notes: Current shop price is preferred for current price; launch price is historical context.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Launch release introduced G1 and gave historical launch pricing and sensor/battery claims.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Current shop price should be preferred for current price.

evidence_items.title: Mass-production version presentation
evidence_items.claim: Unitree presented G1 at the World Robot Conference and described a mass-production version.
evidence_items.notes: Official event/news claim; not customer deployment evidence.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Unitree described a mass-production version at World Robot Conference.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Official company event claim, not customer deployment.

evidence_items.title: Real G1 self-recovery research
evidence_items.claim: A technical paper reported G1 getting up from face-up and face-down falls on flat, deformable, slippery, and sloped surfaces.
evidence_items.notes: Real-hardware research; policy may not ship with product.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Strong evidence for whole-body recovery control.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: Technical paper reports real-G1 self-recovery across postures and surfaces.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Research-policy capability, not necessarily shipped product behavior.

evidence_items.title: RGB-based loco-manipulation research
evidence_items.claim: The VIRAL paper reports RGB-based real-world loco-manipulation experiments on Unitree G1.
evidence_items.notes: Technical research result; verify final publication and metrics before detailed scoring.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Relevant to visual perception and task execution on real G1 hardware.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: VIRAL paper reports RGB-based loco-manipulation experiments on G1.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Research result; final publication and metrics should be rechecked.

evidence_items.title: Tray transport and balancing research
evidence_items.claim: The SteadyTray paper reports tray/object balancing and transport experiments on Unitree G1.
evidence_items.notes: Research result, not default product capability.
evidence_items.arena_relevance: Evidence for coordinated locomotion and manipulation.
evidence_items.supporting_excerpt: SteadyTray paper reports tray/object transport experiments on Unitree G1.
evidence_items.verification_notes: Research result, not default product capability.

evidence_items.title: Structured grasping research
evidence_items.claim: A technical paper reports a foundation-model grasping pipeline on Unitree G1 for workspace positions and a window glue-application task.

researcher_notes.short_verdict_for_arena: Unitree G1 is best treated as an accessible purchasable humanoid research platform with strong academic evidence for specific tasks, but weak commercial deployment proof.
strongest_positive_evidence: Official public price and order page.
Technical papers using real G1 hardware.
Compact biped form and useful research sensor suite.
weakest_or_missing_evidence: No commercial production deployment with output or hours.
No strong built-in conversational autonomy evidence.
conflicting_claims: Current shop lists 13500 USD; launch release gave about 16000 USD excluding tax and shipping.
Current product page uses a 1320 mm standing dimension; launch-era materials may describe height differently.
do_not_overclaim: Do not treat research policies as default shipped behavior.
Do not assume base model includes EDU hands or Jetson Orin.
Do not treat public sale as commercial task deployment.

currentness.currentness_notes: Treated as a current purchasable Unitree platform as of the 2026-05-16 shop/source review; price and stock should be rechecked frequently.

excluded_claims.claim: Base G1 includes EDU dexterous hands, tactile arrays, or Jetson Orin secondary-development compute
excluded_claims.reason: Official product page distinguishes base and EDU configurations.

excluded_claims.claim: Research-policy results are default shipped autonomy
excluded_claims.reason: Academic papers demonstrate external research systems on G1 hardware, not default product behavior.

excluded_claims.claim: Commercial customer deployment with task hours or output
excluded_claims.reason: No named commercial deployment with measurable output was found.

arena_prompt_summary.one_paragraph_summary: Unitree G1 is a current, publicly listed humanoid research platform with strong accessibility evidence and multiple real-hardware research papers. Its commercial deployment proof is weak, and base versus EDU configuration differences must not be merged.
strongest_evidence: Official public price and product specs.
weakest_evidence: No named commercial deployment with output.
known_do_not_credit: EDU-only hardware on the base model.
